research:
How iOS 26/27 app icons work. I re-checked each claim against developer.apple.com's JSON data endpoints (tutorials/data/documentation/...json).
1) Asset catalog (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/configuring-your-app-icon): one 1024x1024 image generates every size. iOS has three styles, Light (Any), Dark and Tinted, set by choosing "Single Size" and then the Appearance. Verbatim: "Provide your tinted app icon as a grayscale image. Provide your dark app icon with a transparent background so the system-provided background can show through." Variants you don't provide get the system's automatic treatment. The Contents.json form uses appearances [{"appearance":"luminosity","value":"dark"}] and the same with value "tinted"; this matches the AccentColor.colorset syntax already in the repo and third-party examples. createwithswift adds that the tinted image should be fully opaque (https://createwithswift.com/preparing-your-app-icon-for-dark-and-tinted-appearance); Apple's page only says "grayscale".
2) Icon Composer `.icon` (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/creating-your-app-icon-using-icon-composer), verified:
- Layers are SVG or PNG. "For layers that contain unsupported SVG features, choose PNG."
- At most four groups. Canvas 1024x1024 for iPhone.
- "Remove blurs and shadows, and specular, opacity, and translucency settings. Remove background colors and gradients."
- "If you add an Icon Composer file to your Xcode project, it replaces any existing icon asset catalog." Also: "You can have multiple Icon Composer files in your project but only one that matches the name in the App Icon text field", and "The latest version of Xcode uses the Icon Composer file instead of an existing AppIcon asset catalog in your project."
- Xcode generates images for older releases at build time.
- "In iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and watchOS versions earlier than 27, specular highlights appear on when you choose Inside or Outside, and Refraction settings have no visible effect." So the owner's iOS 27 phone would show refraction.
- The icon.json schema is not public. A real example, verified by reading the patch (https://lore.proxmox.com/all/DDWMW3GQP9PN.CBBJLTQ7RPK5@proxmox.com/t/), uses these keys: "fill": "system-light"; groups[] {"blur-material": null, layers[], "shadow": {"kind": "layer-color", "opacity": 0.5}, "specular": true, "translucency": {"enabled": true, "value": 0.2}}; layers[] {"blend-mode-specializations": [{"appearance": "dark", "value": "normal"}], "glass": true, "hidden": false, "image-name-specializations": [{"value": "light.svg"}, {"appearance": "dark", "value": "dark.svg"}], "name", "position": {"scale": 0.9, "translation-in-points": [0, 0]}}; "supported-platforms": {"circles": ["watchOS"], "squares": "shared"}.
- Known failures:
  - https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/811935 reports "Icon export exited with status 255, signal 0" plus "unable to open dependencies file (…assetcatalog_dependencies_thinned)". The fix was removing old icon files from Copy Bundle Resources, so an old icon and a .icon side by side can break the build.
  - https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/801388 reports "Could not locate icontool" when Icon Composer is missing from the Xcode bundle.
  - https://dev.classmethod.jp/articles/icon-composer-not-applied/ (2026-05-18) covers an XcodeGen project with no Copy Bundle Resources phase, where the .icon was silently ignored; the fix was `buildPhase: resources`. This repo already has a resources phase (Assets.xcassets), but the generated pbxproj should be checked for `AppIconGlass.icon in Resources`.
3) HIG app icons (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons; change log: "June 8, 2026 Refined guidance for Liquid Glass"), verified:
- "Let the system handle blurring and other visual effects … no need to include specular highlights, drop shadows between layers, beveled edges, blurs, glows."
- iOS appearances are Default, dark, clear light, clear dark, tinted light and tinted dark.
- Size 1024x1024 px. Colour spaces sRGB, Gray Gamma 2.2 or Display P3.
- "Produce appropriately shaped, unmasked layers", "Prefer clearly defined edges in foreground layers … avoid soft and feathered edges".
Adopting Liquid Glass › App icons (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technologyoverviews/adopting-liquid-glass) says the same.
4) XcodeGen CHANGELOG (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen/master/CHANGELOG.md) 2.45.1: "Added built in `.icon` folder support for IconComposer #1600". CI's 2.46.0 includes it.
5) APIs, verified on developer.apple.com (declaration and iOS minimum):
- `func subtracting(_ other: Path, eoFill: Bool = false) -> Path` (iOS 17.0)
- `func union(_ other: Path, eoFill: Bool = false) -> Path` (17.0)
- `func strokedPath(_ style: StrokeStyle) -> Path` (13.0)
- `mutating func addArc(tangent1End: CGPoint, tangent2End: CGPoint, radius: CGFloat, transform: CGAffineTransform = .identity)` (13.0)
- `GraphicsContext.clip(to:style:options:)` (15.0)
- `Canvas.init(opaque:colorMode:rendersAsynchronously:renderer:)` (`nonisolated init`, renderer not @Sendable, 15.0)
- `GraphicsContext.Filter.shadow(color:radius:x:y:blendMode:options:)` (15.0)
- SwiftUI `Path` conforms to Sendable. `Shape` is declared `nonisolated protocol Shape : Sendable, Animatable, View`, which is why the repo's Shapes are `nonisolated struct`.
- UILaunchScreen (iOS 14.0) documents the subkeys UIColorName, UIImageName, UIImageRespectsSafeAreaInsets, UINavigationBar, UITabBar and UIToolbar.

Prototypes by the previous investigator are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PixlAudio/37ceea8f-15b4-5bd4-86db-67f3cfb90817/scratchpad/proto/logo_proto.py, with outputs in ../out/. I viewed sheet_light.png: Concept A clearly reads as the Android icon (compared with ../android_icon.png). The scratchpad may not be visible to the next agent, so all numbers are repeated here.

Shared geometry (1024 grid; every concept uses it):
- Triangle: rounded polygon with sharp vertices TL(204,76), Lpinch(232,512), BL(204,948), R(920,512) and corner radii [120, 3000, 120, 96], built from tangent arcs. Lpinch is indented, so it's a reflex vertex, and r=3000 gives the slightly concave left edge of the Android glyph. I checked that the tangent lengths fit the TL–Lpinch edge: about 230 + 192 < 437. Resulting bbox (219,178)-(831,846), 612x668, w/h 0.916 (Android 0.89), bbox centre x 525.
- Disc: circle centre (506,516), r 166, fully inside the triangle.
- Note head: circle centre (494,548), r 76. It lies entirely inside the disc: centre distance 34, and 34 + 76 < 166.
- Note stem and flag: one rounded polygon [(524,548), (524,278), (690,320), (690,388), (570,358), (570,548)] with radii [0, 12, 24, 24, 10, 0]. (570,358) is a reflex corner. The flag straddles the triangle's top edge, as on Android.
- Mono silhouette = triangle − (disc ∪ (note dilated 22 px)) ∪ note, the same topology as Android new_monochrome.

Concept A, "Prism" (faithful evolution, light; recommended):
- Background: linear (0,0)→(1024,1024), #F5F7FF / #DFE3FF @0.5 / #C7BBFF, plus a white glow circle at (300,230) r470, σ120, 55%.
- Triangle shadow: offset (0,+34), σ40, #3B2FC9 at 30%.
- Triangle body: linear (204,76)→(760,948), #93D3FF / #72A6FF @0.42 / #6A6BFF @0.75 / #6C4FF5.
- Inner shade: (triangle − triangle shifted (−22,−26)), σ18, clipped to the triangle, #3A2FC4 at 35%.
- Specular rim: 9 px inner band, white at 95%, ramped 8%→100% toward the top-left.
- Caustic: band from 14 to 26 px inside the edge, σ5, #C9D4FF at 28%, toward the bottom-right.
- Sheen: white circle at (330,250) r330, σ90, clipped, 22%.
- Disc shadow: (512,538) r166, σ26, clipped, #2E3AA8 at 40%.
- Disc: radial gradient centred (448,452), radius 250, #EAF6FF / #ACDDFF @0.55 / #5FAFFF. Rim 7 px: white at 90% (top-left) and #2F6FD8 at 45% (bottom-right).
- Note: shadow offset (4,12), σ10, #0B2766 at 35%. Fill: vertical linear y278→640, #2B62BE→#14357A. Head highlight: white circle at (470,520) r34, σ14, 25%.
- Dark variant (transparent background): triangle #7CC2FF / #5F8DFF / #5B5BF0 / #5A3FE0, triangle shadow 50%, the rest unchanged.
- Tinted: luminance of the dark variant on an opaque black background.

Concept B, "Midnight Lens":
- Background: radial at (400,330), r900, #33309E / #1D1A66 @0.55 / #0D0C33, plus a #6C4FF5 bloom at (620,640) r380, σ160, 45%.
- Triangle: glass at 62% (#8FD3FF / #6C8CFF / #7A55FF), with a 12 px rim (#C8F0FF / #8FB4FF / #B9A2FF) at 95%.
- Disc: halo r196, σ40, #7FC4FF at 55%; core radial #FFFFFF / #BFE6FF @0.45 / #5E9DFF.
- Note: #1B2F7A → #0E1A4A.

Concept C, "Glyph":
- Background: linear (180,0)→(844,1024), #7CCBFF / #6F8EFF @0.45 / #6C4FF5 @0.8 / #5634D2.
- Glyph: the mono silhouette in white→#DCE4FF, shadow offset (0,22), σ26, #22158A at 30%, 7 px white rim.

options.name: Concept A: Prism (recommended)
options.description: Faithful evolution of the Android icon: the lavender background, the sky-to-indigo play triangle, the light-blue lens disc and the navy note, upgraded with depth (drop shadow, inner shade, top-left specular rim, soft caustic, a frosted lens rim and a note highlight). The dark variant is the same foreground on a transparent background; tinted is its grayscale on black. The in-app marks come from the same geometry: a full-colour tile, plus the mono silhouette for palette-tinted contexts.
options.pros: Clearly the Android logo, done better, so it reads as one brand across platforms. The prototype read well from 1024 down to 40 px. The deepest stop is the brand seed #6C4FF5, which ties it to the app palette.
options.cons: The light lavender background is quieter on the Home Screen than vivid icons. Its baked effects are static, and the HIG says to let the system add specular, shadows and glows; Phase 2 (.icon) fixes that.

options.name: Concept B: Midnight Lens
options.description: A deep indigo radial background with the triangle as translucent glass (62%), a gradient light rim, and a glowing white-to-blue core disc under the navy note.
options.pros: The most premium, Liquid-Glass-feeling look, and dark-mode native. The glowing core stays legible at small sizes.
options.cons: Departs from the Android icon's light look, and blends into dark wallpapers. The dark variant adds nothing new.

options.name: Concept C: Glyph on gradient
options.description: The Android monochrome silhouette (triangle with a disc cut-out and the note) as a white glass glyph on a vivid sky-to-violet gradient, in the style of iOS system icons.
options.pros: One shape for the icon, the in-app mark, tinted and clear. The best Clear and Tinted results and the simplest to port.
options.cons: Drops the colourful disc and note that make the Android icon recognisable, so it's less 'inspired by'.

options.name: Delivery path 1 (recommended now): asset catalog PNGs
options.description: Pillow renders opaque AppIcon.png (Any), AppIcon-Dark.png (transparent background) and AppIcon-Tinted.png (opaque grayscale), wired through Contents.json luminosity appearances.
options.pros: Deterministic, can be authored and previewed without a Mac, no CI risk (the same catalog mechanism AccentColor already uses). Works on Xcode 26.6 and 27.
options.cons: Effects are baked, so there's no dynamic specular or refraction. The system may also add its own edge treatment on iOS 26/27 (unverified).

options.name: Delivery path 2 (optional experiment): Icon Composer .icon
options.description: The same script writes App/AppIconGlass.icon/: an icon.json using only the key set verified in the proxmox example, plus flat layers in Assets/ with no baked effects, in at most 3 groups. project.yml:61 switches the App Icon name to AppIconGlass.
options.pros: Real system Liquid Glass (dynamic specular, refraction on the owner's iOS 27) and proper clear and tinted rendering. XcodeGen 2.46.0 supports `.icon` folders.
options.cons: The icon.json schema is undocumented, nothing can be previewed without a Mac, and there are reported actool failures when old icon files sit next to a .icon (forum 811935). The result is only visible on the phone.

options.name: In-app full-colour mark A (recommended): BrandMark.imageset rendered by make-icon.py
options.description: The script also renders the masked tile (continuous corners, transparent outside) at 64 pt @2x/@3x for the Any and Dark appearances into App/Assets.xcassets/BrandMark.imageset. `BrandMark` is then just `Image("BrandMark")`.
options.pros: Pixel-identical to the Home Screen icon (all effects included), no new drawing code or APIs, and no check needed that a Swift drawing matches the PNG.
options.cons: Raster, so it is sharp only up to about 64 pt (re-render larger if a bigger use appears), and a few tens of KB in the bundle.

options.name: In-app full-colour mark B: Canvas drawing
options.description: The previous plan's `BrandMark` Canvas: gradients, a shadow filter, a clipped stroke rim and a radial disc, replaying BrandMarkGeometry. It skips the caustic, sheen and inner shade.
options.cons: It doesn't match the icon exactly, adds about 100 lines and several drawing APIs, and needs a new demo route (shared files) to screenshot-compare it against the PNG.

recommendedPlan.change:
Rewrite as the single source of truth for the logo. It runs at build time only (Pillow), which AGENTS.md rule 2 allows. Keep `python ci/make-icon.py` with no arguments working, and update the docstring. Pillow is already importable here; if it's missing, run `pip install --target <scratch>/pylib pillow` and set PYTHONPATH.
(1) Constants: the shared geometry and the Concept A palettes from the research field. Draw every shape as 4x-supersampled masks. Rounded polygons use tangent arcs exactly as CG/SwiftUI `addArc(tangent1End:tangent2End:radius:)` does, so Swift can replay the same numbers. For vertex P with neighbours A and B: u1 = unit(A−P), u2 = unit(B−P), θ = acos(u1·u2), tangent distance t = r/tan(θ/2), centre = P + unit(u1+u2)·r/sin(θ/2). Sweep the shorter arc from P+u1·t to P+u2·t; this also covers the reflex corners Lpinch and (570,358). Compute gradients on a 256² grid and upscale bicubic. Make rims from mask − eroded(mask, px), multiplied by a directional ramp (light from the top-left). Erode with MinFilter, or with blur plus threshold.
(2) Default outputs:
- App/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/AppIcon.png: 1024 RGB, opaque, Any appearance.
- AppIcon-Dark.png: 1024 RGBA. The background is fully transparent; only the foreground layers, with the dark palette.
- AppIcon-Tinted.png: 1024 opaque, R=G=B grayscale (luminance of the dark foreground composited on #000000). Save as RGB, not mode L.
- App/Assets.xcassets/BrandMark.imageset: BrandMark@2x.png (128 px) and BrandMark@3x.png (192 px), the Any icon masked to a continuous-corner squircle (radius about 0.2237·side) with transparent corners; BrandMark-Dark@2x.png and @3x.png, the dark foreground on an opaque in-app dark tile (linear #24214F→#100F2B), masked the same way. Contents.json uses idiom universal with scale 2x/3x, and the dark entries add appearances [{appearance: luminosity, value: dark}].
- App/DesignSystem/BrandMarkGeometry.swift: generated, with a header saying it's generated by ci/make-icon.py and must not be edited by hand.
- docs/brand/pixlaudio-icon.png: 512 px masked squircle with transparent corners, for the READMEs.
- Only if the owner wants a launch mark: App/Assets.xcassets/LaunchMark.imageset (the foreground without its tile, transparent, 120 pt at @2x 240 px and @3x 360 px) and LaunchBackground.colorset.
(3) Flags: `--preview DIR` writes a contact sheet of masked light, dark and simulated tinted versions at 1024, 180, 120, 87, 60 and 40 px, plus the mono glyph at 28 px in a 48 px circle; don't commit it. Add `--android RES_DIR` and `--icon-composer DIR` for the optional steps below. Runtime is about 10 s.

Three single-size entries, all with idiom universal, platform ios and size 1024x1024: {filename: AppIcon.png}, {appearances: [{appearance: luminosity, value: dark}], filename: AppIcon-Dark.png} and {appearances: [{appearance: luminosity, value: tinted}], filename: AppIcon-Tinted.png}. Keep info {author: xcode, version: 1}. project.yml:61 stays AppIcon.

`nonisolated enum BrandMarkGeometry` holding static values on the 1024 grid:
- trianglePoints: [CGPoint] and triangleRadii: [CGFloat]
- discCenter and discRadius; headCenter and headRadius
- notePoints and noteRadii; haloWidth 44 (22 px each side)
- glyphFrame CGRect(x: 150, y: 137, width: 750, height: 750), centred on (525,512), so the glyph fills about 89% of its box like Android's 28 dp glyph
Pure Sendable values only. Colour stops are needed only for the Canvas alternative; then store them as 0xAARRGGBB UInt32 and convert with the existing `Color(argb:)` (Theme.swift:27). DesignSystem is a shared folder (design.md:225-227), so commit the two new files on their own with a one-line reason.

(a) Paths: `nonisolated enum BrandMarkPaths` with static lets built once (SwiftUI Path is Sendable).
- `static func roundedPolygon(_ p: [CGPoint], _ r: [CGFloat]) -> Path`: move to the midpoint of the edge (p[n−1], p[0]), then `addArc(tangent1End: p[i], tangent2End: p[(i+1)%n], radius: r[i])` for each vertex, then closeSubpath. Radius 0 is fine for the two hidden note corners.
- triangle; disc = Path(ellipseIn:); note = roundedPolygon(notePoints, noteRadii).union(Path(ellipseIn: head rect)).
- glyph = triangle.subtracting(disc.union(note.strokedPath(StrokeStyle(lineWidth: 44, lineCap: .round, lineJoin: .round)))).union(note).
(b) `nonisolated struct BrandGlyph: Shape`. It must be `nonisolated`: Shape is a nonisolated, Sendable protocol, and under SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION = MainActor a plain struct would make `path(in:)` main-actor isolated (repo pattern: GlassStyle.swift:58, LibraryComponents.swift:275/304). `path(in:)` returns `BrandMarkPaths.glyph.applying(CGAffineTransform(translationX: rect.midX, y: rect.midY).scaledBy(x: s, y: s).translatedBy(x: -525, y: -512))` with s = min(rect.width, rect.height)/750. Fill it with palette roles, so it follows the requested accent picker.
(c) `struct BrandMark: View`: `Image("BrandMark").resizable().interpolation(.high).aspectRatio(1, contentMode: .fit).accessibilityHidden(true)`. This is the full-colour app-icon tile, with fixed brand colours, light/dark from the imageset. If the owner prefers the Canvas alternative instead: copy the colour scheme and the static data into locals before the Canvas closure (WelcomeArt.swift:10-13), use `context.clip(to:)`, `drawLayer` + `addFilter(.shadow(...))` and `.linearGradient` / `.radialGradient` shading, and ledger `GraphicsContext.clip(to:style:options:)`.
In a doc comment, call it logo artwork (like WelcomeArt), not a glass substitute. Never use it as a container background, and never put `glassEffect` on it inside a glass card (no glass on glass). Nothing here matches ci/check-forbidden.sh patterns.

Lines 45-50: replace `Image(systemName: "waveform")…background(theme.primaryContainer, in: Circle())`. Default (Android parity): `BrandGlyph().fill(theme.onPrimaryContainer).frame(width: 28, height: 28).frame(width: 48, height: 48).background(theme.primaryContainer, in: Circle()).accessibilityHidden(true)`. Alternative if Hoa prefers (owner decision): `BrandMark().frame(width: 48, height: 48)`, the app-icon tile. Update the doc comment at :3-4 ("app icon circle") to match.

If yes, keep the title block centred as Android does: wrap only the title VStack (:12-19) in `HStack(alignment: .center, spacing: 14) { BrandMark().frame(width: 64, height: 64); <existing VStack> }`, and keep the existing `.padding(.horizontal, 8).padding(.top, 12)` (:20-21) on the HStack. Don't use a Spacer: it would push the title to the leading edge. Measure on the shots: "Welcome to" at 42 pt plus 78 pt must fit 343 pt (375 pt phones minus 32). If it's tight, put the mark above the title instead. Leave WelcomeArt and the Beta chip untouched.

Line 76: `UILaunchScreen: { UIImageName: LaunchMark, UIColorName: LaunchBackground, UIImageRespectsSafeAreaInsets: true }` (all documented subkeys, iOS 14). This mirrors Android 12+'s system splash showing the icon. LaunchMark.imageset comes from make-icon.py (see above). LaunchBackground.colorset is #F4F6FF light and #000000 dark. recommendedPlan.file: Phase 2, optional, separate branch: App/AppIconGlass.icon/ + project.yml:61
recommendedPlan.change:
Run `make-icon.py --icon-composer App/AppIconGlass.icon`. It writes icon.json using only the keys seen in the verified example:
- top-level "fill": "system-light" (or omit it; the background layer covers it) and "supported-platforms": {"squares": "shared"}
- groups[] {layers, "specular": true, "translucency": {"enabled": true, "value": 0.2}, "shadow": {"kind": "layer-color", "opacity": 0.5}}
- layers[] {name, glass, "hidden": false, "image-name-specializations": [{value}, {appearance: "dark", value}], "position": {"scale": 1, "translation-in-points": [0, 0]}}
Groups and layers:
- Group 1, glass false: 0-Background.png (full-bleed gradient), with a dark specialization 0-Background-Dark.png. Without one, the Dark appearance keeps the light lavender.
- Group 2: 1-Triangle.svg.
- Group 3: 2-Disc.svg and 3-Note.svg.
Use PNG for the background because Apple says to use PNG for unsupported SVG features, and gradient support isn't documented. Foreground SVGs are flat solid fills with crisp edges (HIG): no shadows, rims or blurs. Emit SVG arcs from the same tangent-arc geometry.
Set ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIconGlass.
On CI, check the generated pbxproj lists `AppIconGlass.icon in Resources`.
If actool fails with 'Icon export exited with status 255' or 'unable to open dependencies file … assetcatalog_dependencies_thinned' (forum 811935), the coexisting AppIcon.appiconset is the likely cause. Remove it on that branch rather than keeping it as a fallback; a revert restores it.
Confirm with a CI build, plus an [ipa] build on Hoa's phone.

risks: Baked effects vs system effects: the HIG explicitly says to leave specular, shadows and glows to the system. iOS 26/27 may also add its own edge highlight to a flat asset-catalog icon (unverified), and baked rims could double up with it. Keep the rims subtle and check on the phone in Default, Dark, Clear and Tinted.
Tinted must be opaque grayscale and Dark must have a transparent background, or the system treatments look wrong. Save tinted as RGB with equal channels.
iOS caches Home Screen icons (and launch screens), so after sideloading the new icon may not show until a reboot. Tell Hoa, so it isn't reported as a bug.

Swift 6: BrandGlyph must be `nonisolated struct … : Shape` (Shape is a nonisolated, Sendable protocol; the default MainActor isolation would otherwise isolate path(in:)). BrandMarkGeometry and BrandMarkPaths must be `nonisolated enum` so static lets are usable from path(in:). If the Canvas alternative is used, copy environment values into locals before the renderer closure.
The generated BrandMarkGeometry.swift can drift if hand-edited. The header says to regenerate; the script is the only source.

Path boolean ops (iOS 17) can leave hairline slivers where the halo meets the disc. Build the paths once as static lets and check the 28 pt glyph in the About screenshots. docs/performance.md:52 lists the About appear fade as a known screenshot flake; don't chase it.

Nothing compiles locally, so verify on CI. All new APIs are checked on developer.apple.com (Path.subtracting/union iOS 17, strokedPath/addArc iOS 13, GraphicsContext.clip iOS 15), all below the iOS 26.1 target, so nothing goes in Compat27.swift.

Icon Composer (Phase 2): the icon.json schema is undocumented, nothing can be previewed without a Mac, and builds are reported to fail when old icon files coexist with a .icon (forum 811935) or icontool is missing (forum 801388). Apple says a matching .icon replaces the asset-catalog icon. Keeping AppIcon.appiconset as a 'fallback' next to AppIconGlass.icon is therefore not proven safe: be ready to delete it on that branch.
The raster BrandMark.imageset is sharp only up to the rendered size (64 pt). If a larger in-app use appears (for example 120 pt), re-render at that size rather than scaling up.

Owner rule tension: decision 10 says port, not remake. A new icon and a mark on the welcome page are owner requests that override parity. The About glyph keeps Android's layout (a 48 pt circle with a 28 pt mono glyph), and the welcome title stays centred as on Android.

The Android repo is read-only per AGENTS.md:75 and has two unrelated histories. Any Android change needs Hoa's go-ahead and must target origin/android-int-oct3, which lacks assets/icon.png even though its README references it.
